proposals.evidence: DEDR4635 gives Tamil mañcaḷ, Malayalam maññaḷ/mañña, Kannada mañjaḷa, Kodagu mañja and Tulu mañjaḷu turmeric or turmeric-yellow. The selected simple southern survey mañja/mañjal-type turmeric responses are comparative lect extensions preserving palatal nasal/stop spelling, final-lateral loss and vowel notation; no longer compound is reduced to this stem. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

These simple southern survey forms preserve the corresponding c-/s-/ts- and cēr-/kesar- shapes; minority-lect assignments are comparative extensions, not claims that each lect is individually listed. proposals.evidence: DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaṉ and Malayalam makan/mōn son, Kannada maga/makan, Tulu mage and Toda mox child/son. The selected southern survey makan/magan/maga/mahan-type responses preserve the family, including k/g/h variation and nasalized or nasal-cluster lect forms. These minority-lect assignments are comparative proposals; ambiguous contractions and longer compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR131 explicitly gives Tamil/Malayalam aṇṇan, Kannada aṇṇa/aṇa, Kodagu aṇṇë, Tulu aṇṇe and Konda ana/anasi elder brother. These complete survey forms match that kinship family, retaining final vowels and the Konda relational ending. Nursery-word similarity and the cited Prakrit comparison limit claims about the precise transmission history; compounds and unrelated brother terms are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
